And every person showed interest in his newly built home—THIS house. This location was selected by him for it, as the harbor was visible and the ocean could be heard from here. Out there, he created the garden for his bride, though he was not the one who planted the Lombardies. Mrs. Ned Russell was the one who planted THEM. However, a double line of rose-bushes exists in the garden, which were placed there by the young girls who attended the Glen school for the schoolmaster’s bride. According to him, they were pink like her cheeks, white like her brow, and red like her lips. He had cited poetry to such an extent that I suppose he kind of developed the habit of speaking it as well.

“Nearly everyone gave him a small gift to assist with outfitting the home. Upon entering it, the Russells were wealthy and appointed it truly finely, just as you can observe; however, the initial furnishings that entered it were quite simple. Nevertheless, this small home overflowed with love. Quilts, tablecloths, and towels were contributed by the women, while a chest was crafted for her by one man, and a table by another, and so forth. A small basket was even woven for her from the sweet-smelling sand-hill grass by blind old Aunt Margaret Garrick. For many years, it was utilized by the schoolmaster’s wife for storing her handkerchiefs.

“Well, finally all was prepared—including the logs in the large hearth prepared to be lit. However, it was not precisely THIS fireplace, even if it stood in the identical spot. Miss Elizabeth installed this one when she remodeled the dwelling fifteen years back. You could have roasted an ox in that large, antique hearth. I have sat in this location and told stories many a time, just as I am doing this evening.”

Once more a hush fell, as Captain Saul briefly communed with unseen guests whom Nell and Hugh were unable to perceive—the people who had joined him beside that hearth during bygone times, with laughter and wedding happiness gleaming in eyes that had been shut eternally beneath cemetery turf or rolling expanses of ocean for a very long time. In this spot during former nights young ones had tossed merry laughter back and forth. In this place throughout cold winter nights companions had assembled. Dancing, melody, and witty remarks had existed here. Within these walls young men and young women had indulged in dreams. To Captain Saul the tiny dwelling was filled with figures begging not to be forgotten.

“July’s opening day marked the completion of the dwelling, at which point the schoolmaster commenced his daily tally. Observing him strolling beside the water, we would remark among ourselves, ‘She’ll soon be with him now.’

“Her arrival was anticipated by mid-July, yet she failed to appear at that time. No one experienced concern. Ships were frequently held up for days and perhaps weeks. The Royal William became one week late—and subsequently two—and subsequently three. And eventually we started feeling terrified, and the fear grew steadily more intense. At last I was unable to endure gazing into John Tremayne’s eyes. Do you know, Mistress Carrow”—Captain Saul dropped his tone—“I used to imagine their appearance was identical to how his ancient great-great-grandmother’s must have appeared while she was being burned to death. He rarely spoke a great deal, but he conducted school like someone dreaming and afterward rushed toward the beach. On numerous nights he paced there between nightfall and daybreak. Folks claimed his sanity was slipping. Everyone had abandoned all hope—the Royal William was late by eight weeks. The time was mid-September and the bride of the schoolmaster had not arrived—would never arrive, in our belief.

“A severe gale occurred at that time and persisted for three days, and I walked down to the beach on the evening following its cessation. The schoolmaster was present, resting his folded arms on a large boulder while looking toward the ocean.
“Although I addressed him, no response came from his lips. Something invisible to my own vision appeared to hold his gaze. Fixed like the countenance of a corpse, his face showed no life.
“'John—John,’ I shouted—just in that manner—just like an alarmed youngster, 'wake up—wake up.’
“That peculiar, dreadful expression appeared to somewhat diminish from his eyes.
“His head turned, and his eyes met mine. That face of his has never left my memory—and it never will leave it until the time comes for me to embark on my final journey.

“‘Everything is fine, boy,’ he says. ‘I have observed the Royal William rounding East Point. She is going to arrive here before dawn. By tomorrow evening I am going to be seated with my wife next to my very own hearth-fire.’
“Is it your opinion that he actually saw it?” Captain Saul asked suddenly.
“God knows,” Hugh uttered quietly. “Immense love alongside immense pain could achieve wonders beyond our understanding.”
“I have no doubt that he observed it,” Nell declared with conviction.
“Fol-de-rol,” Doctor Dave remarked, yet his voice carried less certainty than it normally did.
“For, as you are aware,” Captain Saul remarked with gravity, “it was at dawn on the following morning that the Royal William entered Seven Gulls Harbor.

“All the people living in the Glen and by the beach gathered at the ancient pier for her arrival. The teacher had kept vigil at that spot through the entire night. A great shout went up from us when she navigated into the waterway.”

A gleam was in Captain Saul’s eyes. Looking past the present, they beheld the Seven Gulls Harbor as it had been sixty years prior, where a worn, aged vessel voyaged amid the magnificence of the rising sun.
“Was Damaris Leigh among those on board?” Nell inquired.

“Indeed—she along with the spouse of the captain. The voyage they endured was terrible—one storm following another—and furthermore, their supplies ran out. Nevertheless, they finally arrived. As Damaris Leigh set foot upon the ancient wharf, John Tremayne held her close—causing the crowd to cease shouting and start weeping. Even I wept, even if, remember, it was many years before I confessed to it. Isn't it strange how boys feel such shame about crying?”
“Did Damaris Leigh possess beauty?” Nell inquired.

“Indeed, whether you would term her precise beauty—I—do—not—know,” Captain Saul stated unhurriedly. “In a way, one never advanced enough to question if she possessed good looks or lacked them. It simply was irrelevant. A quality so charming and endearing marked her that loving her became inevitable, nothing less. Nevertheless, she presented an agreeable appearance—large, bright, hazel eyes alongside abundant shiny brown hair, plus a complexion typical of the English. That evening when candles were first lit, John and she wed at our dwelling; all the local folk and those from afar gathered there for the event, and collectively we escorted them to this place later. The fire was kindled by Mistress Tremayne, whereupon we departed, leaving the couple seated right where they were, precisely as John had witnessed during his vision. An uncanny occurrence—an uncanny occurrence! Yet I have observed an enormous amount of uncanny occurrences throughout my life.”
Captain Saul gave a wise shake of his head.
“It is a sweet tale,” Nell remarked, experiencing a sense that she had finally received sufficient sentimentality to content herself. “What was the length of time they spent residing in this place?”

“Fifteen years. Like the young scalawag I was, I ran off to sea soon after their marriage. However, every time I arrived back from a voyage, even prior to going home, I’d head for this place and tell Mistress Tremayne all about it. Fifteen happy years! Those two possessed a sort of talent for happiness. If you’ve noticed, some folks are like that. No matter what happened, they COULDN’T remain unhappy for long. Because they was both high-sperrited, they quarrelled once or twice. But laughing in that pretty way of hers, Mistress Tremayne says to me once, says she, 'I felt dreadful when John and I quarrelled, but underneath it all I was very happy because I had such a nice husband to quarrel with and make it up with.’ Afterwards, they relocated to Port Marlow, and Ned Russell purchased this house and brought his bride here. As I remember them, they were a gay young pair. Miss Elizabeth Russell was the sister of Hector. A year or so later, she came to live with them, and she was a creature of mirth, too. Laughing and good times must be sorter SOAKED into the walls of this house. Mistress Carrow—you’re the third bride I’ve seen come here, and the handsomest.”

Captain Saul managed to present his sunflower praise with the subtle grace of a violet, which Nell displayed with pride. That evening saw her appearing her finest, featuring the bridal rose upon her cheeks alongside the love-light in her eyes; even the stern, aged Doctor Dave bestowed a favorable look upon her, remarking to his wife during their shared journey home that the boy’s red-headed spouse possessed a certain beauty.
“It is necessary for me to return to the light,” declared Captain Saul. “This evening has been immensely enjoyable for me.”
“It is necessary that you visit us frequently,” Nell expressed.
“I wonder if you’d offer that invitation if you realized how probable it is that I’ll accept it,” Captain Saul observed with a touch of whimsey.
“Which amounts to saying you question whether I am serious,” Nell smiled. “I am, ‘cross my heart,’ just like we said in our school days.”

“In that case, I will come. It is probable that I will bother you at any time. Furthermore, I will be honored if you come over and see me occasionally, as well. Usually, my only speaking companion is the First Mate, bless his friendly soul. Although he listens extremely well and has forgotten a greater amount than any MacAllister among them ever possessed knowledge of, he does not converse very much. Even though you are young and I am old, I suppose the ages of our souls are nearly identical. As Winifred Tolley would express it, we are both members of the race that knows Joseph.”
“The group that is acquainted with Joseph?” Nell asked in confusion.

“Indeed. Winifred categorizes everyone in the world into two types—the people who understand Joseph and the people who do not. Should an individual more or less agree with you, sharing roughly identical thoughts regarding matters, along with a matching sense of humor—well, in that case, they are part of the people who understand Joseph.”
“Ah, I see,” cried Nell, comprehension suddenly dawning on her.
“It is the phrase—which I continue to place in quote marks—'kindred spirits,' as I once termed it.”

“Precisely—precisely,” Captain Saul concurred. “Whatever IT may be, we are it. Mistress Carrow, as you arrived this evening, I remarked to myself, 'Indeed, she belongs to the lineage that recognizes Joseph.’ And I felt immensely pleased, because had that not been true, we would have been unable to derive any genuine enjoyment from one another’s presence. I believe the lineage that recognizes Joseph constitutes the salt of the earth.”

The moon was newly risen as Nell and Hugh accompanied their guests to the door. Seven Gulls Harbor was starting to turn into a realm of dream, glamour, and enchantment—a charmed port where no storm could ever destroy. Down the lane, the Lombardies, as lofty and grave as the sacerdotal figures of a mystic fraternity, were crested with silver.

“Lombardies have always been favorites of mine,” Captain Saul stated, gesturing toward them with an elongated arm. “Trees for princesses are what they are. Nowadays, people consider them outdated. They object to their tops dying off and becoming shabby. It is true—it is true, provided you fail to jeopardize your safety each spring by ascending a frail ladder to cut them back. My performing this task for Miss Elizabeth ensured that her Lombardies remained pristine. They held a special place in her heart. Their reserved nature and majestic air appealed to her. Every Tom, Rufus, and Harry is denied their friendship. Mistress Carrow, maples provide companionship, but Lombardies offer high society.”
“It is such a lovely evening,” remarked Mrs. Doctor Dave while getting up into the buggy belonging to the Doctor.

“The majority of nights possess beauty,” Captain Saul remarked. “However, I must admit that the moon shining upon Seven Gulls leads me to ponder how heaven could offer anything more. Mistress Carrow, the moon serves as a wonderful companion to me. My affection for her dates back as far as my memory goes. As a young lad aged eight, I drifted off to sleep outdoors in the garden during an evening without being noticed. Waking up during the middle of the night, I felt frightened nearly to the point of dying. The shadows and odd sounds that existed were dreadful! Moving was something I did not dare to do. I simply remained huddling and trembling there, a helpless little creature. It felt as though no other person existed on earth besides me, and the world appeared vast. At that moment, I suddenly observed the moon peering at me via the apple branches, resembling a familiar pal. Relief came over me instantly. I stood and journeyed toward the dwelling as courageous as a lion, keeping my gaze upon her. Countless nights have seen me observing her from the deck of my vessel, traversing waters distant from this place. Is there a reason you people fail to command me to pull in my tongue and return to my house?”

The merriment of the farewells faded into silence. Strolling hand in hand, Nell and Hugh circled their garden. In the birches' shade, the brook flowing through the corner showed clear, shimmering ripples. Resembling delicate goblets of moonlight, poppies lined its borders. Blossoms that the schoolmaster’s bride had set in the earth cast their fragrance into the dim atmosphere, resembling the grace and benediction of holy days gone by. Halting in the darkness, Nell plucked a stem.

“It gives me pleasure to catch the scent of blossoms when it is night,” she stated. “That is when you truly reach their essence. Oh, Hugh, my dreams of this tiny cottage have all come true. And my heart is filled with joy that others before us have shared a newlyweds’ rendezvous in this place!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: At Seven Gulls Harbor, that September brought golden mists and purple hazes—it was a month filled with sun-drenched days and nights that either swam in moonlight or pulsated with stars. Not a single storm ruined it, nor did any harsh wind blow. Nell and Hugh readied their home, wandered along the beaches, navigated the harbor, took drives around Seven Gulls and the Glen, or traveled along the fern-lined, secluded roads in the woods surrounding the harbor head; to put it briefly, they enjoyed a honeymoon that could have made any lovers anywhere jealous.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “If existence was to come to a sudden end right now it would nevertheless have been thoroughly worthwhile, merely on account of these previous four weeks, wouldn’t it?” spoken by Nell. “I do not imagine we shall ever enjoy four so flawless weeks again—yet we HAVE possessed them. All things—wind, weather, people, house of dreams—have joined together to render our honeymoon enchanting. There has not so much as been a wet day since our arrival here.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “And we haven’t fought a single time,” Hugh joked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Indeed, ‘when a delight is postponed, its enjoyment is only amplified,’” recited Nell. “It brings me such joy that this location was chosen for our honeymoon. Rather than being dispersed across unfamiliar spots, the recollections we create will permanently reside right here, within our house of dreams.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: In the air of her new dwelling place, Nell discovered a particular flavor of romance and adventure that had always been absent in Brierley. While she had resided within view of the ocean in her former home, it had never been a close part of her daily existence. At Seven Gulls, however, she was enveloped by it, and it summoned her without ceasing. A different face of the water met her gaze from each window of the house. She continually heard its persistent, gentle hum. On a daily basis, ships navigated up the harbor toward the Glen wharf, or departed amidst the setting sun, heading for destinations that could be located on the opposite side of the world. Each morning, white-sailed fishing vessels glided down the waterway, coming back filled with their catch when night fell. Cheerful and satisfied mariners and fishing people walked along the twisting, red roads of the harbor. One constantly felt that events were about to unfold—that journeys and adventures lay just ahead. Life in Seven Gulls was far less quiet, established, and routine than in Brierley; breezes of transformation swept across the area; the ocean forever beckoned to the people living on the coast, and even the ones who could not respond to its summons experienced its excitement, agitation, secret nature, and endless potential.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “I comprehend now the reason certain men are compelled to head to sea,” remarked Nell. “That longing that strikes every one of us occasionally—‘to sail beyond the bourne of sunset’—is surely immensely commanding when someone is born with it. It does not surprise me that Captain Saul escaped on account of it. Whenever I spot a vessel gliding out of the channel, or a seagull gliding above the sand-bar, I invariably wish that I was aboard that vessel or possessed wings, not in the manner of a dove ‘to fly away and be at rest,’ but in the manner of a seagull, to dart straight into the absolute center of a tempest.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Nell-girl, you will remain right here beside me,” Hugh stated in a relaxed manner. “Flying off into the centers of tempests and away from me is something I will not permit you to do.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: Their position in the late afternoon was upon their red sand-stone doorstep. Land, sea, and sky enveloped them in great tranquillities. Soaring above them were silvery gulls. Long trails of frail, pinkish clouds laced the horizons. A murmurous refrain of minstrel winds and waves threaded the hushed air. In the sere and misty meadows that lay between them and the harbor, pale asters were blowing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Medical men forced to remain awake through the night attending to the ill are not apt to possess a strong sense of adventure, I imagine,” Nell remarked with tolerance. “Had you enjoyed a restful sleep yesterday evening, Hugh, your eagerness for an excursion of fancy would match my own.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “I performed good work during the night, Nell,” Hugh said softly. “With God’s help, I preserved a life. It is the very first instance I could truly make that claim. In different situations I might have assisted; however, Nell, had I failed to remain at Allonby’s during the night and battle death directly, that woman must have perished prior to morning. I attempted a trial that was surely never attempted in Seven Gulls previously. I question whether it was ever attempted anywhere previously beyond a hospital. It was a recent method in Portmaris hospital this past winter. I could not ever have ventured to attempt it here had I not been completely sure that no other hope existed. I took the risk—and it worked. Consequently, a fine wife and mother is preserved for many years of joy and utility. When I traveled home earlier today, as the sun ascended above the harbor, I offered thanks to God for picking the career that I picked. I had waged a fine battle and triumphed—consider it, Nell, TRIUMPHED, against the Great Destroyer. It is the thing I envisioned accomplishing in the past when we conversed with each other about our desires for life. That vision of mine turned into reality earlier today.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Did any of your other dreams end up becoming reality?” inquired Nell, fully aware of what he would reply, yet desiring to listen to it once more.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “IT is clear to you, Nell-girl,” Hugh remarked, a smile meeting her gaze. Just then, a pair of utterly joyful individuals were undoubtedly seated upon the front step belonging to a small, white dwelling along the margin of Seven Gulls Harbor.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: A moment later, Hugh spoke, his voice shifting, “Am I mistaken, or is a full-rigged ship making its way up our lane?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: Nell looked and sprang up.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “That is surely either Mrs. Vane or Miss Winifred Tolley arriving for a visit,” she remarked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “I shall step inside the office, and I give you warning that if Miss Winifred is there, I will listen in,” Hugh remarked. “Based on everything I have been told about Miss Winifred, I gather her talk is bound to be anything but uninteresting.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Perhaps it is Mrs. Vane.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Mrs. Vane does not strike me as being constructed in that manner. chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Unless curiosity brought her, she cannot resemble Mrs. Sowerby,” Nell remarked. “Miss Winifred is who I believe this visitor to be.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: It was indeed Miss Winifred; furthermore, Miss Winifred had not arrived to execute a short and stylish nuptial visit. Her work was cradled beneath her arm inside a solid bundle, and upon Nell’s invitation to remain, she immediately removed her large sun-hat, which a firm elastic band beneath the rigid, tiny bun of her blonde hair had secured to her head, notwithstanding the impudent September gusts. No hat pins were suited for Miss Winifred, if you please! Elastic bands had served her mother sufficiently well, and they served HER sufficiently well. A healthy, circular, pink-and-white complexion belonged to her, alongside cheerful brown eyes. The conventional old maid was not reflected in her appearance at all, and a quality in her countenance captured Nell immediately. Utilizing her long-standing, intuitive speed at identifying like-minded people, she recognized that she would come to fondle Miss Winifred, regardless of unpredictable peculiarities of belief, and undeniable peculiarities of dress.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: Except for Miss Winifred, no one would have arrived to pay a visit dressed in a blue-and-white striped apron alongside a chocolate print wrapper adorned with a pattern of giant, dispersed pink roses. Furthermore, no one except Miss Winifred was capable of appearing stately and appropriately dressed while wearing such attire. If Miss Winifred had been stepping into a royal residence to visit the bride of a prince, her dignity and absolute command of the circumstances would have remained entirely unchanged. She would have dragged her rose-covered ruffle across the marble flooring with equal indifference, and she would have moved forward with identical composure to rid the princess's thoughts of any belief that owning a simple man, whether a prince or a peasant, was something to boast about.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “My task has come along with me, dear Mrs. Carrow,” she observed, spreading out a piece of delicate fabric. “Finishing this quickly is my priority, and not a single moment can be wasted.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: Nell observed the white piece of clothing laid across Miss Winifred’s spacious lap with a degree of astonishment. Unquestionably, it was an infant's gown, and it possessed magnificent craftsmanship featuring minute tucks and frills. Positioning her spectacles, Miss Winifred commenced sewing with extraordinarily fine stitches.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “This is intended for Mrs. Gideon Proctor up at the Glen,” she declared. “Any day now, she is anticipating the birth of her eighth baby, and she does not have a single stitch prepared for it. Whatever she crafted for the first child has been worn out by the subsequent seven, and she has lacked the time, energy, or heart to craft any more. Mark MY words, Mrs. Carrow, that woman is a martyr. I foresaw the outcome the moment she wed Gideon Proctor. He belonged to that class of evil, captivating men. Once married, his captivating nature vanished, leaving only his evil ways behind. He consumes alcohol and ignores his household. Is that not typical of a man? Without the assistance of her neighbors, I have no idea how Mrs. Proctor would manage to keep her children respectably dressed.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: Miss Winifred, as Nell would discover later on, stood alone among the neighbors in concerning herself with the proper conduct of the young Proctors.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “I made up my mind to craft a few items for this eighth child upon learning it was on the way,” Miss Winifred continued. “I am aiming to complete this final one today.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “It is without a doubt extremely lovely,” Nell remarked. “I am going to fetch my needlework so the two of us can hold a small sewing gathering. Miss Tolley, your skill at stitching is marvelous.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Indeed, I am the top needlewoman around here,” stated Miss Winifred with a straightforward demeanor. “It is only natural! My goodness, I have sewn more than I would have if I had birthed a hundred offspring myself, you can take my word for it! I guess I am silly, adorning this garment for an eighth child with manual needlework. However, goodness, Mrs. Carrow, my dear, the child is not at fault for being number eight, and I sort of wanted it to possess a single genuinely lovely gown, exactly as though it WERE desired. No one wants the unfortunate little creature—hence I added additional detail to its small garments for that very reason.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “That dress is something any baby could take pride in,” remarked Nell, experiencing an even deeper conviction that Miss Winifred would be to her liking.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “I imagine you’ve been under the impression that I would never drop by to visit you,” Miss Winifred continued. “However, this happens to be the harvest season, as you are aware, and I’ve been occupied—plus there are numerous additional laborers idling about, consuming more food than the labor they perform, precisely like the men. Initially, I believed my head was throbbing so severely that I wouldn’t be able to enjoy myself even if I attended. chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Did the event go well?” Nell inquired, seeing that the door to the office stood slightly open.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “What is that? Ah, indeed, the funeral was enormous. Her circle of acquaintances was extensive. More than one hundred and twenty carriages joined the procession. A couple of amusing incidents occurred. I believed I would expire from laughter upon witnessing old Joe Bradshaw, an infidel who refuses to enter a church, passionately and fervently belt out 'Safe in the Arms of Jesus’. Singing is his pride and joy—for that reason, he attends every single funeral. Poor Mrs. Bradshaw appeared far from singing—completely exhausted from endless toil. Occasionally, old Joe sets off intending to purchase a gift for her, only to return with a different piece of agricultural equipment. Does that not epitomize a man? Yet what other behavior could one anticipate from a male who avoids church entirely, even a Methodist chapel? It gave me genuine gratitude to spot you alongside the young Doctor attending the Presbyterian church on your inaugural Sunday. I refuse to be treated by any doctor who fails to be a Presbyterian.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Last Sunday evening, we attended the Methodist church,” Nell stated mischievously.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Well, I reckon Dr. Carrow must attend the Methodist church occasionally, otherwise he would lose the Methodist practice.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “The sermon was very much to our liking,” Nell stated courageously. “And in my opinion, the prayer from the Methodist minister was among the most exquisite I have ever listened to.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Oh, there is no question in my mind that he is capable of praying. No one ever produced more lovely prayers in my hearing than old Simon Bentley, who remained perpetually intoxicated, or longed to become so, and his praying improved the more intoxicated he became.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “The Methodist preacher possesses a most handsome appearance,” remarked Nell, directing her words toward the office door.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Indeed, he is rather decorative,” concurred Miss Winifred. “Oh, and EXTREMELY effeminate. Furthermore, he imagines that he enamors any young woman who glances his way—as though a itinerant Jewish-like Methodist clergyman were a great catch! Should you and the young doctor follow MY counsel, you will keep your distance from the Methodists. My principle remains—if you HAPPEN to be a Presbyterian, ACT like a Presbyterian.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Is it not your belief that Methodists reach heaven just like Presbyterians?” Nell inquired, without a smile.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “We are not the ones to make that decision. Unmarried is what THIS Methodist minister happens to be. Married was the previous one they possessed, and I never laid eyes on a creature more foolish and fickle than his spouse. That her husband ought to have delayed marrying her until her adulthood was a piece of advice I once offered him. His response was that he wished to guide her upbringing himself. Is that not just how a man thinks?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “It is quite difficult to determine the exact moment when individuals ARE adults,” Nell laughed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “That’s accurate, dearie. Certain people are already mature at birth, whereas others haven't matured by the time they reach eighty, take MY word for it. chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “It’s possible that explained her long life,” Nell offered.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Perhaps it was. I would prefer to exist for fifty rational years instead of a hundred senseless ones.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Yet only consider how monotonous the world would become if all people were prudent,” begged Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: Miss Winifred held any contest of frivolous witticism in contempt.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Mrs. Roderick belonged to the Milgrave family, and a great deal of sense was something the Milgraves never possessed. For a long period, her nephew, Ebenezer Milgrave, suffered from insanity. His delusion was that he had passed away, and he frequently flew into rages at his wife for refusing to inter him. I’d a-done it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: Miss Winifred appeared so fiercely resolved that Nell was nearly able to picture her holding a spade.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Are there NOT any good husbands you know, Miss Tolley?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Oh, yes, lots of them—over yonder,” Miss Winifred said, gesturing with her hand out the open window in the direction of the small church graveyard situated across the harbor.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Yet being alive—moving around in a body?” insisted Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Oh, to demonstrate that every single thing can be done through God, a handful exist,” Miss Winifred admitted unwillingly. “I will not dispute that a rare male scattered here or there might become a respectable creature, provided he is taken while young, raised correctly, and thoroughly disciplined by his mother in advance. YOUR husband, at present, is not terribly awful, compared to other men, based on everything I am told. I imagine”—Miss Winifred peered intently at Nell across her spectacles—“you believe no one else on earth compares to him.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “There is not,” Nell replied without delay.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Ah, well, I listened to a different bride express that on a past occasion,” Miss Winifred uttered with a sigh. “Upon her marriage, Jennie Dean believed that no one in existence compared to HER husband. Her assessment was correct—no such person existed! Furthermore, take MY word for it, that was fortunate! The existence he forced upon her was terrible—and as Jennie was on her deathbed, he was already pursuing his next spouse.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Is that not typical of a man? Nevertheless, my hope is that YOUR faith proves more well-founded, dearie. The youth who is a doctor is catching on very well. My initial fear was that he might not, because the people in these parts have forever considered old Doctor Dave as the sole doctor anywhere. To be certain, Doctor Dave lacked much tact—he constantly brought up ropes in dwellings where a person had committed suicide. Yet people overlooked their injured sentiments whenever their stomachs pained them. Had he served as a minister rather than a doctor, forgiveness would never have been granted to him. A aching soul causes people far less concern than a aching stomach. Since the two of us are Presbyterians with no Methodists present, would you share with me your honest view regarding OUR minister?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Why—really—I—well,” Nell stammered.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: Miss Winifred gave a nod.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Precisely. My sentiment aligns with yours, my dear. Calling HIM was an error on our part. Does his visage not resemble one of those elongated, slender headstones in the cemetery? His brow should be inscribed with 'Sacred to the memory.’ The initial discourse he delivered upon his arrival remains etched in my memory. The topic concerned each person engaging in the work for which they are best suited—undoubtedly an excellent topic; yet the examples he cited were astonishing! He remarked, 'If you had a cow and an apple tree, and if you tied the apple tree in your stable and planted the cow in your orchard, with her legs up, how much milk would you get from the apple tree, or how many apples from the cow?’ Have you ever encountered such a thing in all your life, my dear? It brought me great relief that no Methodists were present that day—their mockery would have been endless. However, my chief grievance regarding him is his tendency to concur with everyone, regardless of what is stated. Should you tell him, 'You’re a scoundrel,’ he would respond, accompanied by that bland grin, 'Yes, that’s so.’ A pastor ought to possess greater fortitude. Ultimately, I regard him as an ordained fool. Naturally, this remains strictly between the two of us. In the presence of Methodists, I laud him immensely. Certain individuals believe his spouse wears attire that is overly vibrant, yet my view is that cohabiting with a countenance like his warrants something to brighten her spirits. I will never be heard criticizing a female regarding her garments. My heart is simply grateful when her spouse is not so stingy and parsimonious as to forbid it. Not that I devote much attention to clothing personally. Females merely attire themselves to gratify males, and I would refuse to demean myself to THAT extent. My existence has been genuinely tranquil and pleasant, my dear, entirely because I never valued the opinions of men in the slightest.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “What makes you despise the men to such a degree, Miss Tolley?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Lord, honey, I lack hatred for them. They do not deserve it. I merely rather hold them in contempt. I believe I will care for YOUR husband should he persist in the manner he started. chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “To be sure, Captain Saul is marvelous,” Nell concurred warmly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Captain Saul is a decent chap, though he’s somewhat irritating in a single regard. You simply CANNOT get him angry. I’ve attempted it for two decades, yet he continues to remain calm. chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “What was her identity?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Well, I am uncertain, my sweet. Captain Saul courting anyone is something I have no recollection of. As long as I can recall, he was getting on in years. As you are aware, seventy-six is his age. Why he remained unmarried was never explained to my knowledge, yet I assure YOU a cause exists. Up until five years back, he spent his whole existence at sea, exploring every single nook of the world. Throughout their existence, he and Elizabeth Russell maintained a deep friendship, yet romantic intentions were never present between them. Despite numerous opportunities, Elizabeth never wed. During her youth, her beauty was remarkable. Her uncle, a Government official residing in Port Marlow, hosted her as a guest during the year the Prince of Wales visited the Island, which led to her receiving a ball invitation. No girl present surpassed her in looks, leading the Prince to dance with her, an act that enraged every unchosen woman whose higher societal rank caused them to claim he ought not to have ignored them. That particular dance remained a point of immense pride for Elizabeth. Spiteful individuals claimed this explained her refusal to marry—that having danced with royalty, a common man would no longer suffice. That claim, however, was false. The true cause was once disclosed to me by her—she possessed such a fierce disposition that she feared peaceful cohabitation with any husband would be impossible. Indeed, her temper was terrible—occasionally, to control it, she was forced to retreat to her room above and sink her teeth into the furniture. Nevertheless, I informed her that such a flaw should not prevent her from wedlock if she desired it. We ought not to allow men to hold a monopoly on bad tempers, wouldn't you agree, my dear Mrs. Carrow?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “My own patience is somewhat short-lived,” Nell let out a sigh.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “It is good that you possess it, my dear. You will stand much less chance of being stepped upon, trust ME! Goodness, the way your golden glow is flourishing! The garden you have looks magnificent. Poor Elizabeth used to tend to it so meticulously.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “I love it,” Nell said. “I’m happy it has so many old-fashioned flowers. chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Indeed, Henry Rudge over at the Glen takes on those sorts of tasks. Perhaps he will suffice. He is forever far more concerned with his pay than his labor, precisely like a male, and he is so sluggish to comprehend that he remains motionless for five minutes prior to realizing he has halted. His father launched a log at him during his youth.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “That was a lovely, soft rocket, wasn’t it? Just like a man would do! Naturally, the lad didn’t ever recover. Nevertheless, he is the single person I am able to endorse whatsoever. Last spring, he did the painting on my house. Don't you agree that it appears truly lovely at present?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: It was the five o'clock chime of the clock that rescued Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “My goodness, has it reached that hour already?” Miss Winifred cried out. “When a person is having fun, the hours really do fly! Oh well, I ought to head back to my house.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “No, certainly not! You will remain and join us for tea,” Nell exclaimed enthusiastically.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Do you inquire of me since you believe you must, or owing to your genuine desire?” inquired Miss Winifred.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “In that case, I shall remain. YOUR people are the ones who recognize Joseph.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “I am certain that a friendship will form between us,” Nell remarked, accompanied by the specific expression that was revealed solely to those belonging to the household of faith.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Indeed, we do, dearie. Thank heaven, selecting our friends is within our power. Our relatives must be accepted as they come, and we should be grateful when none of them are jailbirds. chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: A tone of yearning was present in the voice of Miss Winifred.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “I want you to address me as Nell,” Nell blurted out with sudden emotion. “It would feel extra HOMEY that way. chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “I am fond of Nell. My mother was called that. In my view, traditional names are the finest and most charming. Should you be fetching tea, you could ask the young doctor to come speak with me. chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “How did you know?” exclaimed Nell, who was far too shocked by this example of Miss Winifred’s weird foresight to offer a courteous disavowal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL
text: “Upon walking up the path, I spotted him seated next to you, and I am well aware of how men behave,” Miss Winifred countered. “Well, I have completed my tiny garment, darling, and the arrival of the eighth child can happen whenever it wishes.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: The promised visit to Seven Gulls light was finally made by Nell and Hugh toward the end of September. Although they had frequently intended to make the trip, various obstacles continually arose to hinder them. At the small home, Captain Saul had “dropped in” on a few occasions.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Mistress Carrow, I am not one for formal manners,” he informed Nell. “Visiting this place brings me genuine joy, and I refuse to deprive myself simply on account of your not coming downstairs to meet me. Among those of us who understand each other, such conditions shouldn't exist. My visits will happen whenever possible, and yours will too, and provided that our agreeable small talk takes place, the particular shelter above us is of no consequence whatsoever.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Captain Saul developed a strong fondness for Gog and Magog, who ruled over the hearth's fortunes in the small dwelling with the same degree of grace and composure as they had displayed at Tabby’s Place.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Aren’t they the cutest little cusses?” he used to inquire with delight; and with as much seriousness and regularity as he addressed his host and hostess, he offered them his greetings and goodbyes. Captain Saul had no intention of insulting domestic spirits through a deficit of veneration and formality.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “This small home of yours is nearly flawless now,” he remarked to Nell. “In the past, it was never this lovely. Mistress Tremayne possessed a style like yours and accomplished marvelous things; yet people back then lacked the lovely small drapes, artwork, and ornaments that belong to you. Regarding Elizabeth, her existence was bound to former times. In a way, you’ve sort of introduced what lies ahead to this place. If conversation were entirely impossible for us when I visit, I’d still be truly joyful—simply remaining seated to gaze at you, along with your art and your blooms, would provide a sufficient pleasure. Beautiful—it’s just beautiful.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Captain Saul possessed a fervent adoration for beauty. His existence was illuminated by a profound, delicate, interior delight derived from every beautiful sight or sound. Feeling a sharp consciousness regarding his personal absence of physical attractiveness, he mourned it.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “People claim I have talent,” he mused playfully on a certain day, “yet I occasionally desire that the Lord had created me merely half as talented and allocated the remainder to my appearance. Even so, I suppose He understood His business, just as a capable Captain ought to. A few of us are required to be plain, or else the attractive individuals—such as Mistress Carrow right here—would not stand out so effectively.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Eventually, Nell and Hugh strolled down to the Seven Gulls light during one evening. Gray cloud and mist had made for a gloomy start to the day, which nevertheless concluded with a magnificent display of gold and scarlet. Amber depths and clear, crystalline shallows lay above the western hills on the far side of the harbor, underpinned by the sunset’s blaze. Fiery little golden clouds formed a mackerel sky across the north. Gliding along the channel toward a southern port in a tropical palm country, a ship's white sails caught the glowing red light. Farther off, this illumination struck and turned blood-red the gleaming, white, vegetation-free surfaces of the sand dunes. Off to the right, it touched the ancient dwelling amidst the willows along the brook, briefly bestowing upon it windows more magnificent than those found in an old cathedral. Amid its serenity and drabness, they shone like the pulsating, crimson thoughts of a vibrant mind trapped inside a dreary shell of surroundings.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “The ancient dwelling further up the stream continually appears so solitary,” Nell remarked. “I do not ever observe guests in that place. To be sure, its driveway leads out to the top thoroughfare—yet I do not believe there is a great deal of traffic. It appears strange that we have not hitherto encountered the Vanes, considering they reside less than a quarter-hour’s stroll from our home. Naturally, I might have caught sight of them at chapel, though had that occurred I failed to recognize them. I regret that they prove so distant, given that they represent our sole close neighbors.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “It seems they aren't part of the group that recognizes Joseph,” Hugh chuckled. “Did you ever discover the identity of the young woman you considered so lovely?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “No. For some reason I have failed to inquire concerning her. Since I’ve never caught sight of her anywhere, though, I assume she was likely an unfamiliar face. Oh, the sun has only now disappeared—and the light has appeared.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: With the advancing twilight, broad beams were carved through the gloom by the massive lighthouse, rotating continuously across the meadows, the haven, the shoal, and the open sea.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “It seems capable of seizing me and carrying me miles across the ocean,” Nell remarked, when a wave of brightness soaked them; and reaching a position so close to the Point that they were positioned within the radius of those blinding, repeating beams gave her a sense of relief.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: When they made the turn into the small lane leading to the Point through the fields, they encountered a man exiting it—a person whose look was so remarkable that both of them stared openly for a second. Tall, broad-shouldered, and with good features including a Roman nose and open gray eyes, he was unquestionably handsome; wearing a wealthy farmer’s finest Sunday clothes, he could, to this extent, have belonged to Seven Gulls or the Glen. However, a river of wavy brown beard cascaded down his chest almost reaching his knees, while a matching deluge of dense, rippling brown hair hung down his back from under his ordinary felt hat.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Nell,” whispered Hugh, as soon as they had moved beyond hearing distance, “did you happen to pour what Uncle Dave terms 'a little of the Scott Act’ into the lemonade you handed me right before we departed from the house?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Indeed, I did not,” replied Nell, holding back her chuckles so the departing mystery wouldn't overhear. “Whatever person could he possibly be?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “I am uncertain; however, should Captain Saul maintain phantoms of that nature at this Point, carrying a piece of cold iron in my pocket will be my practice upon visiting. His lack of being a sailor prevents one from excusing his peculiar look; he ought to be a member of the over-harbor clans. According to Uncle Dave, a number of freaks reside in that place.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “My opinion is that Uncle Dave holds a slight bias. As far as you are aware, every individual from over the harbor attending the Glen Church appears quite pleasant. Oh, Hugh, doesn’t this look lovely?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: A projection of red sandstone precipice extending into the gulf served as the site for the Seven Gulls light. Extending across the channel on one flank lay the bar’s silvery sand shore; stretching along the opposite side was a lengthy, sweeping beach of red cliffs, which ascended sharply from the pebbled coves. Magic and mystery belonging to storm and star were familiar to this shore. A profound solitude exists around a coast like this. Solitude is never found in the woods—they overflow with whispering, beckoning, welcoming life. Conversely, the sea represents a mighty soul, perpetually lamenting a grand, unshareable grief, which confines it within its own existence for all eternity. Piercing its boundless mystery is impossible for us—we can merely roam, awed and spellbound, along its outermost border. A hundred voices call to us from the woods, whereas the sea possesses just one—a mighty voice that submerges our souls inside its majestic music. Human nature belongs to the woods, yet the sea resides among the ranks of the archangels.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Nell and Hugh discovered Uncle Saul as he sat on a bench outdoors by the lighthouse, completing the final details of a magnificent, fully rigged toy schooner. Standing up, he greeted them at his dwelling with the soft, natural politeness that suited him so perfectly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Every part of this day has been fairly lovely, Mistress Carrow, and currently, at its very end, the finest portion has arrived. Would you care to be seated out here for a short time, while daylight remains? Just now, I completed this small toy for Joe, my tiny grand nephew, up at the Glen. Subsequent to my agreement to construct it for him, I felt rather regretful, because his mother was annoyed. She fears he will desire to head out to sea in the future, and she prefers that the idea not be fostered within him. Nevertheless, what choice did I have, Mistress Carrow? I had PROMISED him, and to my mind, breaking a pledge made to a youngster is somewhat truly despicable. Come, take a seat. Spending an hour here will not require much time.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Off the shore, the wind blew, doing no more than fracturing the ocean's face into lengthy, silvery ripples and causing gleaming shadows to hurry across it from each point and headland, resembling see-through wings. Over the headlands, where gulls gathered together, and the sand dunes, twilight suspended a veil of violet darkness. Scarves of silky mist thinly coated the sky. On the horizons, fleets of clouds floated at anchor. Above the bar, an evening star kept guard.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Is that not a sight that merits a look?” inquired Captain Saul, showing an affectionate, possessive pride. “It is comfortably distant from the market-place, is it not? No purchasing or vending or turning a profit. You are not charged a single cent—that entire expanse of ocean and firmament is costless—‘without money and without price.’ Furthermore, a moonrise will occur very shortly—discovering what a moonrise is capable of being above those rocks and water and harbor is something I never grow weary of. Each occasion contains an element of surprise.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: They observed the moon rise, taking in the wonder and enchantment of it silently, requiring nothing from one another or the world. After that, they climbed to the tower, where Captain Saul displayed and detailed how the large light's machinery operated. At last, they ended up in the dining room, in which a driftwood fire was creating flickering, subtle, ocean-tinted flames within the open hearth.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “I built this hearth with my own hands,” Captain Saul observed. “Those in charge do not provide lighthouse keepers with these kinds of comforts. Notice the hues produced by that wood. Should you desire any driftwood for your hearth, Mistress Carrow, I will haul a supply up to you one of these days. Take a seat. I am preparing to brew a cup of tea for you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Captain Saul set down a seat for Nell, but only after he had cleared off a massive, orange-hued cat along with a newspaper.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Step down, Matey. Your spot is the sofa. I have to store this paper securely until I am able to locate the time for completing its tale. A Mad Love is its title. This kind of story is not my preferred type, yet I am only reading it to observe the extent to which she can prolong it. The sixty-second chapter has been reached, and from what I can tell, the marriage is not a bit closer than it was at the start. I must recite pirate tales to little Joe whenever he arrives. Isn't it odd that harmless young ones such as kids enjoy the most bloodthirsty tales?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Just like Robin, my boy back home,” Nell remarked. “He desires stories dripping with blood.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Captain Saul’s tea turned out to be nectar. Nell’s compliments made him as happy as a child, though he feigned a fine indifference.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “My secret is that I am generous with the cream,” he nonchalantly observed. Captain Saul was unacquainted with Oliver Wendell Holmes, yet he clearly shared the perspective of that author's assertion that “big heart never liked little cream pot.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “While drinking, Hugh remarked, “A strange-looking individual was walking out of your lane when we encountered him.” “Who could he be?””

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: A smirk appeared on Captain Saul's face.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Ambrose Kerr is that fellow—an exceptionally grand person who possesses merely a single strain of silliness. It crosses my mind that you were curious about his motive for making himself resemble a kind of cheap side-show oddity.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Does he represent a contemporary Nazarite, or is he an ancient Hebrew prophet remaining from long ago?” Nell inquired.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “It is neither. Politics lies behind his oddity. Every one of those Kerrs, Crawfords, and MacAllisters is a politician through and through. Depending on the situation, their birth makes them Grit or Tory, their life is spent as Grit or Tory, and as Grit or Tory they pass away; and I cannot begin to understand what they will manage in heaven, where politics likely does not exist. Ambrose Kerr here entered the world as a Grit. As for me, I am a moderate Grit, yet moderation is something Ambrose lacks. A particularly fierce general election occurred fifteen years back. Tooth and nail, Ambrose campaigned for his side. He held absolute confidence in a Liberal victory—confidence so complete that he stood before a public gathering and swore he would avoid shaving his face or trimming his hair until power belonged to the Grits. Well, victory eluded them—and they have failed to achieve it to this day—and what you witnessed today was the consequence. Ambrose kept his promise.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “How does his wife feel about it?” inquired Nell.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “He isn't married. However, if a wife existed, I suppose she wouldn't be able to force him to violate that promise. The members of that Kerr family have constantly shown a resolve that exceeds what is natural. The brother of Ambrose, Alexander, possessed a dog that he valued immensely, and upon its death, the man truly desired for the animal to be interred within the cemetery, 'along with the other Christians,’ he stated. Naturally, permission was denied; consequently, he placed its grave right beyond the fence of the cemetery, and he refrained from ever crossing the church threshold again. Nevertheless, on Sundays he would transport his household to the church and remain seated near the grave of that dog, reading from his Bible throughout the duration of the service. People claim that as he was passing away, he requested that his spouse inter me near the dog; she possessed a timid, quiet nature, yet THAT made her spark with anger. She declared SHE refused to lie buried next to any dog, and if he preferred his final bed to be by the dog instead of by her, he only needed to state it. Alexander Kerr possessed the obstinacy of a mule, yet he cherished his spouse, so he yielded and stated, 'Well, durn it, bury me where you please. But when Gabriel’s trump blows I expect my dog to rise with the rest of us, for he had as much soul as any durned Kerr or Crawford or MacAllister that ever strutted.’ Those were HIS final spoken statements. Regarding Ambrose, everyone around here has grown accustomed to him, though he bound to appear extremely odd-looking to outsiders. My acquaintance with him began when he was ten years old—his age is roughly fifty currently—and I hold him in high regard. He and I were on the water cod-fishing today. That activity represents nearly everything I can manage these days—hooking the occasional trout and cod. Yet things were not always like this—definitely not in any way. I engaged in different pursuits in the past, a fact you would concede if you were to view my life-book.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: As Nell was on the verge of inquiring about the nature of his life-book, the First Mate caused a distraction by leaping onto Captain Saul’s knee. A magnificent creature, he possessed a face resembling a full moon in roundness, striking green eyes, and huge, double white paws. Captain Saul softly petted his velvety back.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Cats were never much to my liking until I came across the First Mate,” he observed, as the Mate purred exceedingly loud. “His life was saved by me, and a creature becomes impossible not to love once you have saved its life. Doing so is almost like bestowing life itself. The world contains some dreadfully unthinking individuals, Mistress Carrow. Certain city people owning summer residences across the harbor possess such a lack of thought that it amounts to cruelty. That unthinking variety is the most terrible form of cruelty. Coping with it is impossible. They maintain cats at those places throughout the summer, offering them food and affection, and decorating them with collars and ribbons. Then, upon the arrival of fall, they depart and abandon them to perish from hunger or cold. Mistress Carrow, my blood boils because of it. On a single day during this past winter, I discovered a miserable old mother cat lying dead upon the beach, her body pressed against her three tiny kittens who were nothing but skin and bone. Her death had occurred while attempting to protect them. Around them were wrapped her poor, rigid paws. I wept, Master. After that, I uttered curses. Following that, those poor little kittens were brought home by me, given plenty of food, and provided with good homes. The identity of the woman who abandoned the cat was known to me, and upon her return during the present summer, I simply crossed the harbor and expressed my view of her directly. My action was blatant interference, yet interfering for a worthy cause is something I truly enjoy.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “In what manner did she react?” inquired Hugh.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “She wept and mentioned that she ‘didn’t think.’ I told her, I says, ‘Is that going to be considered a proper justification on the day of Jedgment, when you are required to answer for the life of that poor old mother? I suppose the Lord will inquire why He bestowed brains upon you if they were not meant for thinking.’ I doubt she will abandon cats to die of hunger on another occasion.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Did the First Mate belong to the forsaken?” inquired Nell, offering him friendly overtures that he answered in a gracious, albeit patronizing, manner.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Yes. HIM I discovered on a freezing winter day, trapped in tree branches by his foolish ribbon collar. He had nearly starved. Mistress Carrow, if only you could have witnessed his eyes! Being merely a kitten, he had managed to survive on his own after being abandoned until he became entangled. Upon my freeing him, his tiny red tongue gave my hand a pathetic lick. The able seaman present today was not what he was then. As Moses, he was meek. Nine years have passed since that time. For a cat, his life in the land has been lengthy. The First Mate is a good old pal.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “I ought to have anticipated that you would possess a dog,” Hugh remarked.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: A shake of his head came from Captain Saul.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “A dog belonged to me once. My regard for him was so great that I was unable to endure the idea of replacing him with a new one after his death. A FRIEND was what he was—is that clear to you, Mistress Carrow? Matey is merely a pal. Matey has my affection—which is all the greater because of the hint of mischief inside him—as exists within every cat. My dog, however, possessed my LOVE. Alexander Kerr always had my secret compassion regarding HIS dog. A fine dog contains no devil at all. They are more worthy of love than cats for that reason, I suppose. Yet I'll be hanged if their interest equals a cat's. Look at me, speaking excessively. What stops you from stopping me? My speech flows terribly whenever an opportunity to converse with somebody comes my way. Provided your tea is finished, I possess some small items that may interest you to view—I acquired them in the strange places where I used to pry.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: The “few little things” belonging to Captain Saul proved to be a deeply fascinating assortment of curiosities—some grotesque, some peculiar, and some lovely. Furthermore, a remarkable tale was tied to nearly single one of them.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: The joy with which Nell heard those ancient stories on that moon-drenched night beside that spellbinding drift-wood flame was something she would always remember, as the silver ocean beckoned to them via the unclosed window and wept upon the stones beneath them.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Captain Saul did not utter a single proud word, yet one could not avoid perceiving what an incredible hero the individual had proven to be—courageous, faithful, clever, selfless. Sitting there within his small room, he brought those events back to life for those who listened to him. Through an eyebrow's elevation, a lip's contortion, a motion, or a spoken word, he depicted an entire event or person in such a manner that they perceived it precisely as it occurred.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: A few of Captain Saul’s exploits possessed so extraordinary a quality that Hugh and Nell privately questioned whether he might be stretching the truth to take advantage of their trusting nature. However, as they subsequently discovered, they misjudged him in this regard. Every one of his stories was factually accurate. Captain Saul possessed the innate talent of a natural narrator, through which “unhappy, far-off things” are able to be conjured brightly for the listener in every bit of their original grief.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: His stories made Nell and Hugh laugh and tremble, and at one point tears came to Nell’s eyes. As Captain Saul observed her crying, delight radiated from his countenance.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “I enjoy watching people weep in that manner,” he observed. “It pays a tribute. However, I am unable to do proper justice to the events I have witnessed or assisted in. I have written them all down in my life-book, yet I lack the skill to draft them correctly. Should I manage to find precisely the correct words and arrange them appropriately on paper, I could create a remarkable book. It would completely outdo A Mad Love, and I reckon Joe would enjoy it every bit as much as the pirate tales. Indeed, I have experienced several adventures during my life; and, tell me, Mistress Carrow, I continue to crave them. Indeed, despite how aged and worthless I am, a terrible yearning overcomes me occasionally to set sail out—out—out there—for all time.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Like Ulysses, you would

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Navigate past the sundown and the waters where every western star sets, right up to your death,’”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Nell uttered in a dreamy manner.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Ulysses? His story is one I’ve read. Indeed, that accurately describes my emotions—exactly how every old seaman among us feels, I suppose. It seems I’m destined to pass away on dry land, I guess. Ah well, whatever happens is meant to happen. Consider old William Treleaven over at the Glen, who avoided going out on the water his entire existence due to his fear of drowning. A fortune-teller’s prophecy had foretold that fate for him. Then one day, losing consciousness, he collapsed face-first into the barn trough and drowned. Is it time for you to leave? Well, visit again quickly and visit frequently. The physician should be the one conversing on our next meeting. A great deal of information I wish to learn is known to him. I feel rather lonely in this place occasionally. The situation has deteriorated since Elizabeth Russell passed away. She and I were such close companions.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: Captain Saul expressed himself with the sorrowful emotion typical of the elderly, who observe their former companions gradually drifting away—companions who can never be truly replaced by individuals from a younger era, even those belonging to the group that recognizes Joseph. Nell and Hugh pledged that they would visit shortly and frequently.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “Isn’t he a rare old fellow?” Hugh asked while they were walking home.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “In some way, I am unable to align his gentle, easygoing nature with the reckless, daring existence he has led,” Nell reflected.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “You would not consider it quite as difficult had you observed him recently in the lower fishing village. A member of Peter Gautier’s vessel uttered an unpleasant comment regarding a local young woman. Captain Saul almost incinerated the miserable man with the fierce glare of his eyes. He appeared to be a completely altered individual. His words were few—yet the manner in which he delivered them! It seemed powerful enough to peel the skin off the man's frame. I gather that Captain Saul does not permit any disparaging remark about any woman to be uttered near him.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: “I am curious why marriage never occurred for him,” Nell uttered. “He ought to possess sons whose vessels are currently out on the ocean, along with grandkids scrambling all over him to listen to his tales—that is the sort of person he is. Rather, he possesses merely a grand cat.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT
text: However, Nell was wrong. Captain Saul possessed something beyond that. A memory was also his.

“I’m going for a walk to the outside shore tonight,” Nell said to Gog and Magog one evening in October. Because Hugh had crossed the harbor, there was nobody else for her to inform. Her small domain was in the spotless organization to be anticipated of anyone raised by Thirza Abernethy, and Nell believed she might head toward the shore with a unburdened mind. Her excursions to the shore had been numerous and wonderful, at times alongside Hugh, at times alongside Captain Saul, and at times by herself with her own reflections and fresh, keenly-sweet dreams that were starting to bridge existence with their rainbows. She cherished the mild, vaporous harbor shore as well as the silvery, wind-frequented sand shore, yet she cherished the rock shore most of all, with its precipices and caverns and heaps of wave-eroded boulders, along with its coves where the pebbles gleamed beneath the pools; and it was toward this shore that she traveled tonight.

A three-day autumnal tempest of rain and gale-force winds had passed. The breakers had smashed against the rocks with a deafening sound, the pale foam and spray had swept wildly across the bar, and the previously tranquil blue waters of Seven Gulls Harbor had become agitated, hazy, and battered by the storm. Now that the weather had cleared, the coastline appeared thoroughly cleansed by the gale; the air was completely still, yet an impressive swell persisted, crashing against the rocks and sand in a magnificent froth of white—the sole motion amid the vast, all-encompassing quiet and serenity.

“Oh, this is a moment worth living through weeks of storm and stress for,” Nell exclaimed, joyfully casting her distant look over the churning waves from the summit of the precipice where she was standing. Soon she climbed down the sharp incline toward the small bay beneath, where she appeared enclosed by stone, ocean, and firmament.
“I intend to perform a dance and a song,” she stated. “No person exists in this place to observe me—the seagulls will not report news about it. My behavior can be as wild as I desire.”

Gathering up her skirt, she twirled past the firm band of sand right beyond the arrival of the waves, whose exhausted froth nearly touched her feet. Spinning repeatedly while laughing in the manner of a child, she arrived at the small promontory extending east from the cove; thereupon she halted abruptly, turning bright red; she lacked privacy; a spectator had observed her dancing and laughing.

Perched upon a rock on the promontory, partially concealed by an overhanging crag, sat the young woman possessing golden hair and eyes the color of the ocean. Her gaze was fixed directly upon Nell, displaying a peculiar countenance that combined astonishment, compassion, and—could that truly be?—jealousy. Wearing no hat, her magnificent tresses, resembling Browning’s “gorgeous snake” to an even greater degree, were secured around her brow by a scarlet band. She was attired in a dark-colored gown of extremely simple design; nevertheless, wrapped around her midsection, accentuating its beautiful lines, was a bright sash of red silk. Though her hands, locked above her knee, were tanned and slightly roughened by labor, the flesh of her neck and face remained cream-white. A swift ray of the setting sun pierced a low cloud in the west, illuminating her locks. In that instant, she appeared to embody the soul of the ocean itself—encompassing its every enigma, its full intensity, and its entire fleeting fascination.

“You—you must think me crazy,” stammered Nell, attempting to regain her composure. It was really too bad to be caught by this regal girl indulging in such a childish outburst—she, Mrs. Dr. Carrow, who had all of a married woman's poise to maintain!
“No,” the girl replied, “I do not.”

She uttered no further words; her tone lacked any emotion; her demeanour was somewhat off-putting; nevertheless, an expression in her eyes—at once keen and hesitant, rebellious and beseeching—prevented Nell from carrying out her intention to leave. Rather than departing, she took a seat on the rock next to the girl.

“Let us state our names,” she remarked, using the grin that had always succeeded in gaining trust and goodwill. “My name is Mrs. Carrow—and my home is that small white dwelling further along the harbor coast.”
“Indeed, I am aware,” the girl stated. “My name is Lorna Vane—Mrs. Rufus Vane,” she appended in a formal tone.

Absolute astonishment kept Nell quiet briefly. That the girl had a husband had never crossed her mind—she appeared to possess no spousal traits whatsoever. Furthermore, that she was the exact neighbor Nell had envisioned as an ordinary Seven Gulls homemaker! Nell struggled to rapidly shift her perspective to accommodate this incredible transformation.
“So—so the gray house farther up the stream is where you reside,” she faltered.
“Indeed. My visit to you ought to have been paid a considerable time back,” the second speaker remarked. No justification or apology for her failure to do so was tendered by her.

“It is my desire that you WOULD pay a visit,” uttered Nell, regaining a degree of composure. “Our proximity as neighbors dictates that friendship should exist between us. The singular defect of Seven Gulls lies in that very aspect—the neighbors are slightly too few in number. In all other respects, it embodies perfection.”
“Is it to your liking?”
“LIKE it! I adore it. It is the loveliest location I have ever seen.”
“I have not visited many locations,” Lorna Vane uttered, unhurriedly, “however, I have constantly believed that this place was extremely beautiful. I—I adore it, as well.”

Her speech matched her appearance, being delivered with a mixture of timidity and enthusiasm. It struck Nell curiously that this unusual girl—she could not help thinking of her as a “girl”—was capable of revealing much more if she wished.
“I frequently visit the coast,” she continued.
“I agree,” Nell remarked. “We should have crossed paths in this place prior to now.”

“It is likely that your visits occur at an earlier hour in the evening than mine. My arrivals are usually late—nearly dark. Furthermore, my favorite time to arrive is right after a storm—resembling this one. The ocean pleases me less when it is still and serene. What I enjoy is the struggle—along with the crash—and the noise.”

“In every one of its states, I adore it,” Nell stated. “What Linger Lane represented back home is what the ocean at Seven Gulls means to me. It appeared so unchained—so fierce—this evening that my own spirit untethered itself as well in harmony. For that reason, I leaped beside the water in such an untamed manner. Naturally, I never imagined that a single soul was watching. Had Miss Winifred Tolley caught sight of me, she’d have predicted a bleak future ahead for the unfortunate young Dr. Carrow.”

“Do you know Miss Winifred?” Lorna asked, chuckling. Her laugh was exquisite; it surfaced all at once and unpredictably, possessing much of the delightful charm found in a baby’s. Nell joined in the laughter, as well.
“Oh, yes. On multiple occasions, she has come down to my house of dreams.”
“The residence you dream of?”
“Ah, Hugh and I use that beloved, silly small moniker for our residence. We merely utilize it when it is just the two of us. It escaped my lips before I realized.”

“Thus the small white home belonging to Miss Russell is THE home of your dreams,” Lorna stated in amazement. “A home of dreams was once mine—however, it was a palace,” she inserted, laughing in a way whose sweetness was spoiled by a slight tone of mockery.

“Oh, I formerly had dreams about a palace, as well,” Nell remarked. “I imagine every girl does.
